THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County moved to put the Hub City Wind Project on hold pending a formal Alliant Energy proposal, while county officials also unveiled a proposed 2027 budget that trims the tax rate by a penny even as average bills tick up.

  • Marathon County Board approved Resolution 55-26, directing Alliant Energy to submit a draft proposal addressing community concerns about the Hub City Wind Project by November 1.
  • Marathon County's HR Finance & Property Committee unanimously accepted a proposed 2027 budget featuring a 1-cent tax rate reduction and a $3.5 million allocation toward a new healthcare facility; amendment deadline is October 7.
  • The Kronenwetter Village Board unanimously approved the Green Tree Trails subdivision preliminary plan — 60-plus one-acre lots with private wells and septic — after significant public comment.
  • Marathon County's Health and Human Services Committee authorized the health department to apply for up to $150,000 in state PATH program funding to support homeless individuals with severe mental illness.
  • Wausau's Board of Public Works approved a $2.1 million payment to Community Infrastructure Partners for ongoing lead service line replacement work.
  • Weston's Comprehensive Plan Steering Committee selected draft vision statement 'C' as its working document and set a public workshop for November 12.

Coming up: The Weston Village Board of Trustees and the Wausau Finance Committee both meet Monday, with Wausau's Finance Committee reconvening Tuesday and Wednesday as well; Marathon County's Executive and Infrastructure committees meet Thursday afternoon.
